results.title: Gaming Accessibility: Making Browser Games Playable for Everyone
results.content: Gaming accessibility ensures that people with disabilities can enjoy video games alongside everyone else. For browser games, accessibility is both a moral imperative and a practical advantage — accessible games reach larger audiences and often provide better experiences for all players. results.title: Accessibility in Browser Games: Who Could Play and Who Got Left Out ...
results.content: The most prevalent accessibility failure in browser games was the action game. Platformers, shooters, rhythm games, and arcade-style titles were built around the assumption that players could react within hundreds of milliseconds and execute precise inputs under time pressure.

results.title: Browser Game Accessibility: Colorblind Modes, Remappable Keys, and ...
results.content: Screen Readers and Non-Visual Play Full screen reader support for an action game is a genuinely hard problem, and most browser games reasonably do not attempt it for real-time gameplay. But menus, instructions, settings screens, and turn-based or text-driven games are a different story.

results.title: Browser Games with Screen Reader Support - Dinogame GG
results.content: Screen reader support in browser games is rare and inconsistent. The format itself is friendly — HTML and ARIA were built to be accessible — but most game developers don't expose game state to assistive technology.
